content.title: About
content.content: Steak teriyaki is a piece of beef marinated in a teriyaki sauce made from soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger, then quickly seared over high heat. The result is tender meat with a sweet‑salty aroma characteristic of Asian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Teriyaki originates from Japan, where the sauce was used to give dishes a glossy, slightly sweet flavor.
Traditional teriyaki sauce is made without corn starch, though many commercial versions use thickeners.
Marinating beef in teriyaki sauce enhances flavor and makes the meat more tender.
In Japan, steak teriyaki is often served with rice, vegetables, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
There is a pineapple‑infused teriyaki variation that adds extra sweetness and aroma.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The iron in beef is highly bioavailable and helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Steak teriyaki supplies vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from soy sauce
items.content: Soy sauce in the teriyaki glaze contains phenolic compounds with antioxidant activity.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Ginger and garlic, often added to teriyaki, have anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce is salty, so people with hypertension should limit portion size.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Teriyaki sauce is frequently sweetened, which can increase the dish’s calorie count.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy sauce.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Commercial sauces may contain preservatives and flavor enhancers that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Marinate the steak in teriyaki sauce for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours). Then sear it on a hot pan or grill for 2–3 minutes per side to the desired doneness. Let the meat rest for 5 minutes, slice thinly, and serve with rice, vegetables or a salad, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked steak teriyaki in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Uncooked beef in the marinade can be kept in the fridge for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze in a separate bag; it will retain quality for up to 2 months.
